corneille-oeuvres-marty-laveaux-t3:
Paris printers Lahure produced tome three of the Marty-Laveaux Corneille for the great-writers series. The edition again reviews the oldest printings and the author's own copies. Old spelling is kept, and verses are numbered by fives as before.

Middle years of Corneille's long career fill this volume. The aging master tried new forms, even grand plays with flying gods and stage machines. All the while, the young Racine was rising fast around him. These plays show a restless mind refusing to repeat past triumphs. He still commanded the stage with skill, even as fashion shifted beneath him toward a leaner and fiercer style.
kindred-sayings-part3:
F. L. Woodward took over the Kindred Sayings with Part Three in 1925. His English version continues the great themed set of discourses. Sutta by sutta, the Samyutta Nikaya unfolds its ordered teaching.

Grouped sayings treat feeling, perception, and the mind's own workings here. The Buddha answers monks and wanderers in brief, pointed exchanges. Woodward keeps the tone plain and the pace of talks brisk. The Pali Text Society's long labor moves steadily through the canon. This middle part rewards readers who read the whole set in order. Themes set up earlier return here with new depth and force.
